topics.label: Course introduction and learning outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: It introduces the lecture series, outlines key learning outcomes, and sets the clinical and biological scope of the course.

topics.label: Cancer as a failure of genetic regulation and tissue differentiation
topics.groupedBecause: They examine the core biological concept of cancer as an accumulation of mutations leading to a breakdown in cellular differentiation and tissue architecture.

topics.label: Tumor invasion, metastasis, and benign-to-malignant progression
topics.groupedBecause: They describe the physical, histological, and stepwise characteristics that distinguish benign growths from invasive and metastatic malignancies.

topics.label: Tumor nomenclature and mechanisms of clinical pathology
topics.groupedBecause: They outline the standard naming conventions for tumors and detail the physiological mechanisms by which tumors cause illness and mortality.

topics.label: Tumor incidence across tissues and species
topics.groupedBecause: They examine the incidence patterns and tissue distributions of tumors in human populations and across diverse multicellular animal species.

topics.label: Principles and applications of cancer screening
topics.groupedBecause: They evaluate the clinical rationale, histological basis, and relative effectiveness of screening methods across various tumor types.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion and practical reminders
topics.groupedBecause: It concludes the lecture with a review of learning objectives and reminders for upcoming practical sessions.
